└── packages/
    └── web/
        ├── opencode.json
        └── src/

### Return a cleanup function from setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Return a cleanup function to release resources owned by the plugin. The example subscribes to session.execution.succeeded and returns a function that stops the subscription.

```typescript
setup(context) {
  const stop = context.data.on("session.execution.succeeded", () => {})
  return () => stop()
}
```

### Set custom installation directory with OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR or XDG_BIN_DIR

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

The install script respects $OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR first, then $XDG_BIN_DIR, then $HOME/bin, and falls back to $HOME/.opencode/bin. Use these examples to override the installation path.

```bash
# Examples
OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
XDG_BIN_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

### Define a basic plugin with setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

Plugins under `.opencode/plugins/` are loaded automatically. The `setup` function runs when the plugin loads and can perform initialization tasks.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.storage.set("loaded", true)
  },
})
```

### Access setup context properties

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

The setup function receives configuration, app metadata, the current location, the OpenCode client, cached data, theme tokens, the OpenTUI renderer, and UI APIs. Use context.options for plugin options and context.data.location.default() as a fallback location.

```typescript
setup(context) {
  const compact = context.options.compact === true
  const location = context.location ?? context.data.location.default()
  const version = context.app.version
  const channel = context.app.channel
  const client = context.client
  const renderer = context.renderer
  const theme = context.theme
}
```

--------------------------------

### Find instances with SelectorOptions examples

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-code-connect/references/api.md

Usage examples for finding instances by specific hierarchy path or traversing all nested instances.

```javascript
// Find icon only in specific hierarchy
const icon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  path: ['Header', 'Actions', 'IconSlot']
})

// Search everywhere including nested instances
const anyIcon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  traverseInstances: true
})
```

### Define extension setup function

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-extensions/README.md

Implements synchronous extension setup using typed context to access dependencies, loaded stores, translations, and contribute commands to the registry.

```ts
const setup: Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  const changes = ctx.uses.changes // Accessor<Live<Changes>>
  const prefs = ctx.stores.prefs.value // loaded before setup
  ctx.add(Command, { id: "open", title: ctx.t("open"), run: () => ctx.layout.settings(ctx.id) })
}
```

### Install OpenCode via curl script and package managers

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

Use the curl script for a quick install, or choose a package manager like npm, brew, pacman, paru, mise, or nix. Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

```bash
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix
```

--------------------------------

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Illustrates building a baseline catalog from immediate sources while background fibers activate slower plugins asynchronously.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Catalog.layer creates empty catalog state
    → PluginBoot.layer activates immediately available plugins
      → ConfigProviderPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → ModelsDevPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → AuthPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
    → Catalog.layer applies active transforms during boot
    → apply policy
    → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Catalog.transform()
      → transform(updateCatalog)
        → Catalog internally rebuilds
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

### Create a keymap layer after an await in setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Call layer from setup, including after an await, or from a component. The layer is removed when the plugin is disabled, reloaded, fails setup, or when the creating component is disposed.

```ts
async setup(context) {
  const settings = await loadSettings()
  context.keymap.layer(() => ({
    mode: "global",
    commands: [{ id: "acme.sync", title: "Sync Acme", palette: true, run: () => sync(settings) }],
  }))
}
```

### Build and run desktop startup benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/desktop/README.md

Builds the desktop application with electron-builder and executes startup benchmark commands under various configurations, such as warm/cold services, A/B comparisons, and profiling flags.

```bash
OPENCODE_CHANNEL=dev bun run build && bunx electron-builder --win --dir --config electron-builder.config.ts
bun run bench:startup -- --runs 5                                  # warm service (started once, reused by every launch)
bun run bench:startup -- --runs 5 --compare dist/other/OpenCode\ Dev.exe   # A/B: alternate launches of two builds
bun run bench:startup -- --service cold                            # each launch spawns the service
bun run bench:startup -- --fresh                                   # first launch after an install (profile wiped each time)
bun run bench:startup -- --profile-main --profile-renderer --trace # CPU profiles and a Chromium startup trace
bun run bench:startup -- --seed "%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop.dev"   # restore tabs and drafts from an existing profile
```

### TextNode Range Methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

SDK methods on TextNode for getting and setting properties across a specific character range (start to end indices).

```APIDOC
## TextNode Range Methods

### Description
Methods available on `TextNode` instances to apply mixed styling, fonts, fills, hyperlinks, and list options to specific character ranges.

### Methods
- `textNode.setRangeFontName(start, end, fontName)`
- `textNode.setRangeFontSize(start, end, size)`
- `textNode.setRangeFills(start, end, fills)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextDecoration(start, end, decoration)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextCase(start, end, textCase)`
- `textNode.setRangeLetterSpacing(start, end, spacing)`
- `textNode.setRangeLineHeight(start, end, lineHeight)`
- `textNode.setRangeHyperlink(start, end, hyperlink)`
- `textNode.setRangeListOptions(start, end, listOptions)`
- `textNode.setRangeIndentation(start, end, indentation)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontName(start, end)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontSize(start, end)`

### Usage Examples
```javascript
// Make "Hello" bold (characters 0-5)
textNode.setRangeFontName(0, 5, { family: 'Inter', style: 'Bold' });

// Make "World" red (characters 6-11)
textNode.setRangeFills(6, 11, [{ type: 'SOLID', color: { r: 1, g: 0, b: 0 } }]);

// Change size of "World"
textNode.setRangeFontSize(6, 11, 24);

// Get properties for a range
const fontAtStart = textNode.getRangeFontName(0, 1);
const sizeAtEnd = textNode.getRangeFontSize(10, 11);
```
```

### Support V1 and V2 from the same package entrypoint

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

Default export one object with a V1 `server()` function and a V2 `setup()` function. V1 calls `server()` and uses the returned hooks. V2 reads the default export's `id` and `setup()` (or `effect()` for Effect plugins), ignoring `server()`. Keep each implementation on its own API; sharing an export does not translate V1 hooks into V2 hooks. Spread `Plugin.define(...)` into the exported object so it type-checks the V2 definition separately from `server()`. The V1 object form is supported in OpenCode `1.18.29`. Older V1 releases may expect function exports instead; test the installed package with the oldest V1 release you intend to support and with V2.

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Starting and connecting to a local service instance with Service.ensure

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Imports the native Promise service API and initializes an OpenCode client connected to a running or newly started background service.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"
import { Service } from "@opencode/client/service"

const endpoint = await Service.ensure()
const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: endpoint.url,
  headers: Service.headers(endpoint),
})

const info = await client.server.info()
```

### Configure Virtual Framebuffer for Headless Environments

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/bs/troubleshooting.mdx

```bash
apt install -y xvfb
# and run:
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1024x768x24 > /dev/null 2>&1 &
export DISPLAY=:99.0
```

### Manage command-based connection attempts

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

Use this to start, check status, or cancel a command-based connection attempt for an integration. The example uses the 'acme' integration with the 'cli' method.

```typescript
const attempt = await ctx.integration.command.connect({ integrationID: "acme", methodID: "cli" })
const status = await ctx.integration.command.status({ integrationID: "acme", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
await ctx.integration.command.cancel({ integrationID: "acme", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
```

### Start and resume queued image generation with Black Forest Labs

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/ai/README.md

Demonstrates starting a generation process with Image.start, persisting its token, and resuming polling in another process with Image.resume. The token does not carry route identity, so persist the provider and model ID alongside it.

```ts
import { BlackForestLabs, Stability } from "@opencode/ai/providers"

const bfl = BlackForestLabs.configure({ apiKey: process.env.BFL_API_KEY })

const submit = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const generation = yield* Image.start({ model: bfl.image("flux-2-pro"), prompt, size: "1024x768" })
  persist({ provider: "black-forest-labs", modelID: "flux-2-pro", token: generation.token })
})

const finish = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const saved = load()
  const resumed = yield* Image.resume(bfl.image(saved.modelID), saved.token)
  return yield* resumed.await({ poll: { interval: "2 seconds" } })
})
```

### List and get agents using Effect

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use this to read all agents or fetch a specific agent by ID. The example logs the count of agents and the name of the 'build' agent.

```typescript
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const agent = ctx.agent
    const agents = yield* agent.list().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const build = yield* agent.get({ agentID: Agent.ID.make("build") }).pipe(Effect.orDie)
    yield* Effect.logInfo("agents", { count: agents.data.length, build: build.data.name })
  }),
```

--------------------------------

### Wildcard pattern matching on resource in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/policies.mdx

Applies a wildcard pattern using * to match zero or more characters in the resource ID. This example denies any provider starting with company-.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "experimental": {
    "policies": [
      {
        "effect": "deny",
        "action": "provider.use",
        "resource": "company-*"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Install Clipboard Utility for Wayland on Linux

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/bs/troubleshooting.mdx

### Create an OpenCode client and start a session

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Instantiate an OpenCode client with OpenCode.make and invoke resource methods like session.create and session.prompt.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"

const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:4096",
})

const session = await client.session.create({
  location: { directory: "/workspace" },
})

await client.session.prompt({
  sessionID: session.id,
  text: "Review the current changes",
})
```

### Manage OAuth connection attempts

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

Use this to start, check status, complete, or cancel an OAuth connection attempt for an integration. The example demonstrates the full flow for the GitHub integration.

```typescript
const attempt = await ctx.integration.oauth.connect({ integrationID: "github", methodID: "oauth" })
const status = await ctx.integration.oauth.status({ integrationID: "github", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
await ctx.integration.oauth.complete({ integrationID: "github", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID, code })
await ctx.integration.oauth.cancel({ integrationID: "github", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
```

### List and get providers using Effect

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use this to read all available providers or fetch a specific provider by ID. The example logs the count of providers and the name of the 'anthropic' provider.

```typescript
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const provider = ctx.provider
    const providers = yield* provider.list().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const anthropic = yield* provider.get({ providerID: Provider.ID.make("anthropic") }).pipe(Effect.orDie)
    yield* Effect.logInfo("providers", {
      providers: providers.data.length,
      anthropic: anthropic.data.name,
    })
  }),
```

--------------------------------

### List available models and default selection

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use ctx.model.list() to retrieve all available models and ctx.model.default() to get the currently selected model. The example logs the count and selected model name.

```typescript
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const model = ctx.model
    const models = yield* model.list().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const selected = yield* model.default().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    yield* Effect.logInfo("models", { count: models.data.length, selected: selected.data?.name })
  }),
```

--------------------------------

### Add a custom LSP server with command and extensions

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/lsp.mdx

Define a new LSP entry by specifying the startup `command` array and the file `extensions` the server should handle.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "custom-lsp": {
      "command": ["custom-lsp-server", "--stdio"],
      "extensions": [".custom"]
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Store, read, and remove JSON values with Effect storage

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use ctx.storage to set, get, and remove durable JSON values scoped to the plugin ID. The example sets a settings object, retrieves it, logs it, and removes it.

```ts
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const storage = ctx.storage
    yield* storage.set("settings", { strict: true })
    const settings = yield* storage.get("settings")
    yield* Effect.logInfo("settings", { settings })
    yield* storage.remove("settings")
  }),
```

--------------------------------

### List and inspect integrations and active credentials

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

Use this to retrieve a list of integrations, get details for a specific integration, check the active connection, and resolve the credential for that connection. The example shows how to access the integration context methods.

```typescript
const integrations = await ctx.integration.list()
const github = await ctx.integration.get({ integrationID: "github" })
const connection = await ctx.integration.connection.active("github")
const credential = connection ? await ctx.integration.connection.resolve(connection) : undefined
```

### Configure and start opencode server instance

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/sdk.mdx

Pass custom configuration options such as hostname, port, and model settings inline to override defaults or opencode.json.

```javascript
import { createOpencode } from "@opencode-ai/sdk"

const opencode = await createOpencode({
  hostname: "127.0.0.1",
  port: 4096,
  config: {
    model: "anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
  },
})

console.log(`Server running at ${opencode.server.url}`)

opencode.server.close()
```

--------------------------------

### Scan storage keys by prefix with cursor pagination

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use storage.scan with a prefix and limit to retrieve entries. The example scans for keys starting with 'cache/', then uses the next cursor to fetch the next page, and logs the total count.

```ts
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const storage = ctx.storage
    const first = yield* storage.scan({ prefix: "cache/", limit: 100 })
    const second = first.next
      ? yield* storage.scan({ prefix: "cache/", after: first.next, limit: 100 })
      : { entries: [] }
    yield* Effect.logInfo("cache entries", { count: first.entries.length + second.entries.length })
  }),
```

### Read VCS repository information and status

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx

Use this to read repository information, working-copy status, branches, and file diffs. The example shows how to access the VCS service from the context and call methods like get, branches, status, and diff.

```typescript
effect: (ctx) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const vcs = ctx.vcs
    const info = yield* vcs.get().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const branches = yield* vcs.branches({ search: "feature", limit: 10 }).pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const changes = yield* vcs.status().pipe(Effect.orDie)
    const diff = yield* vcs.diff({ mode: "working", context: 3 }).pipe(Effect.orDie)
    yield* Effect.logInfo("vcs", { branch: info.data.branch.current, files: changes.data.length })
  }),
```

--------------------------------

### Plugin lifecycle with cleanup function

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx

`setup` runs when the plugin loads. It may return a cleanup function that runs when the plugin unloads.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  setup(ctx) {
    console.log(`loaded in OpenCode ${ctx.app.version}`)
    return () => console.log("unloaded")
  },
})
```

Creates a main process store that loads synchronously and imports initial state from a desktop settings key.

```ts
// The saved hosts, which main keeps; stored before in the desktop settings file.
servers: Store.main(Schema.Array(SshConfig), [], { settings: "ssh.servers" }),
```

### Configure and request completions with ZAI and ZAICodingPlan

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/ai/README.md

Demonstrates initializing ZAI and ZAICodingPlan providers and making LLM requests with model selection and reasoning options. Automatically reads ZAI_API_KEY if omitted.

```ts
import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"
import { ZAI, ZAICodingPlan } from "@opencode/ai/providers"

const zai = ZAI.configure({ apiKey: process.env.ZAI_API_KEY })
const request = LLM.request({
  model: zai.model("glm-5.3"), // also zai.chat("glm-5.3")
  prompt: "Explain this design.",
  providerOptions: {
    reasoningEffort: "high",
    thinking: { type: "enabled", clear_thinking: false },
  },
})

const coding = ZAICodingPlan.configure({ apiKey: process.env.ZAI_API_KEY })
const messages = LLM.request({
  model: coding.messages("glm-5.3"),
  prompt: "Explain this design.",
  providerOptions: { effort: "high" },
})
```

```APIDOC
## ctx.integration.command.connect

### Description
Starts a command-based connection attempt for an integration.

### Method
`command.connect`

### Parameters
#### Input Parameters
- **input** (IntegrationCommandConnectInput) - Required - Contains `integrationID` and `methodID`.
- **requestOptions** (RequestOptions) - Optional - Additional options for the request.

### Response
Returns a Promise resolving to `IntegrationCommandConnectOutput`.

const attempt = await ctx.integration.command.connect({ integrationID: "acme", methodID: "cli" })
```
```

### OpenCode.make(options)

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Instantiates a new OpenCode client instance configured with the server URL, optional default headers, and a custom fetch implementation.

```APIDOC
## OpenCode.make(options)

### Description
Creates and configures an OpenCode client instance to communicate with an OpenCode server.

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Configuration options for the client.
  - **baseUrl** (string) - Base URL of the OpenCode server.
  - **headers** (object, optional) - Default HTTP headers included with requests (e.g., authorization).
  - **fetch** (function, optional) - Custom fetch implementation.

### Example
```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"

const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:4096",
  headers: {
    authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OPENCODE_TOKEN}`,
  },
})
```
```

--------------------------------

### Configure custom provider with apiKey, headers, and limits in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx

Advanced configuration example setting environment-based API keys, custom headers, and model context/output token limits.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "myprovider": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "My AI Provider Display Name",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://api.myprovider.com/v1",
        "apiKey": "{env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}",
        "headers": {
          "Authorization": "Bearer custom-token"
        }
      },
      "models": {
        "my-model-name": {
          "name": "My Model Display Name",
          "limit": {
            "context": 200000,
            "output": 65536
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Video.start(options)

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/ai/README.md

Submits a video generation job and returns an active generation handle for explicit tracking and token persistence.

```APIDOC
### Method Signature
`Video.start(options)`

### Description
Initiates a video generation task asynchronously without awaiting completion, returning a Generation handle with status, IDs, and resume tokens.

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Required
  - **model** (VideoModel) - Required - Selected provider model
  - **prompt** (string) - Required - Text prompt describing the video
  - **aspectRatio** (string) - Optional - Aspect ratio
  - **resolution** (string) - Optional - Resolution
  - **durationSeconds** (number) - Optional - Duration in seconds
  - **providerOptions** (object) - Optional - Provider-specific options

### Returns
An Effect resolving to a `Generation` handle containing:
- **id** (string) - Provider operation, task, or request ID
- **status** (string) - Current status (`"queued" | "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "expired"`)
- **token** (object) - Route-owned JSON used to resume generation
```

### Return a cleanup function in plugin setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/README.md

Returns a cleanup callback from setup that OpenCode awaits when the plugin is unloaded or replaced.

```ts
setup: async (ctx) => {
  const timer = setInterval(refresh, 60_000)
  return () => clearInterval(timer)
}
```

--------------------------------

### createOpencode([options])

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/sdk.mdx

Creates an instance of opencode, starting both a server and a client. Accepts optional configuration parameters for host, port, timeout, abort signaling, and inline server config.

```APIDOC
## createOpencode([options])

### Description
Creates an instance of opencode, starting both a server and a type-safe client.

### Syntax
```javascript
import { createOpencode } from "@opencode-ai/sdk"

const { client, server } = await createOpencode(options)
```

### Parameters
#### Options
- **hostname** (`string`) - Optional - Server hostname. Default: `"127.0.0.1"`
- **port** (`number`) - Optional - Server port. Default: `4096`
- **signal** (`AbortSignal`) - Optional - Abort signal for cancellation. Default: `undefined`
- **timeout** (`number`) - Optional - Timeout in ms for server start. Default: `5000`
- **config** (`Config`) - Optional - Configuration object to customize behavior. Default: `{}`

### Returns
- **client** - Type-safe client instance for interacting with the opencode server.
- **server** - Server instance object providing server management properties and methods, such as `url` and `close()`.

### Usage Example
```javascript
import { createOpencode } from "@opencode-ai/sdk"

const opencode = await createOpencode({
  hostname: "127.0.0.1",
  port: 4096,
  config: {
    model: "anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
  },
})

console.log(`Server running at ${opencode.server.url}`)

opencode.server.close()
```
```

### Get and set focused slide on PageNode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-slides/references/slide-properties.md

Get or set the currently focused slide on a page using the focusedSlide property on PageNode.

```javascript
// Get the focused slide
const focused = figma.currentPage.focusedSlide;
if (focused) {
  return { focusedSlideId: focused.id, name: focused.name };
}

// Set the focused slide
const slide = figma.getNodeById("SLIDE_ID");
figma.currentPage.focusedSlide = slide;
```

### Define project instructions in AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/ar/rules.mdx

An example AGENTS.md file configuring project structure, code standards, and monorepo conventions for an SST v3 project.

```markdown
# SST v3 Monorepo Project

This is an SST v3 monorepo with TypeScript. The project uses bun workspaces for package management.

## Project Structure

- `packages/` - Contains all workspace packages (functions, core, web, etc.)
- `infra/` - Infrastructure definitions split by service (storage.ts, api.ts, web.ts)
- `sst.config.ts` - Main SST configuration with dynamic imports

## Code Standards

- Use TypeScript with strict mode enabled
- Shared code goes in `packages/core/` with proper exports configuration
- Functions go in `packages/functions/`
- Infrastructure should be split into logical files in `infra/`

## Monorepo Conventions

- Import shared modules using workspace names: `@my-app/core/example`
```

### Define main process extension setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-extensions/README.md

Configures power saving controls and manages remote access CLI service calls via the Pairing contract. Releases active display sleep blockers upon scope finalization.

```ts
import { execFile } from "node:child_process"
import { powerSaveBlocker } from "electron"
import type { MainSetup } from "../sdk/main"
import { Pairing } from "./contract"
import type definition from "./index"

/** The display sleep blocker this instance holds, if any. */
type Blocker = { id?: number }

/** The last `opencode service` command; the next one starts after it settles. */
type Queue = { tail: Promise<unknown> }

const setup: MainSetup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  const stored = ctx.stores.keepScreenActive
  const cli = ctx.cli
  const log = ctx.log
  const blocker: Blocker = {}
  const queue: Queue = { tail: Promise.resolve() }

  const release = () => {
    if (blocker.id === undefined) return
    powerSaveBlocker.stop(blocker.id)
    blocker.id = undefined
  }

  const keepScreenActive = (enabled: boolean) => {
    if (enabled && blocker.id === undefined) blocker.id = powerSaveBlocker.start("prevent-display-sleep")

    if (!enabled) release()
    stored.set(enabled)
  }

  // Remote access is a setting of the background service, so it changes through the CLI the app runs, as with
  // `opencode pair --remote`. A change restarts the service, so commands run one at a time.
  const service = (args: readonly string[], signal: AbortSignal) => {
    const run = queue.tail.then(
      () =>
        new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
          execFile(
            cli.command[0] ?? "opencode",
            [...cli.command.slice(1), "service", ...args],
            { signal, windowsHide: true },
            (error, stdout, stderr) => {
              if (!error) return resolve(stdout.trim())
              log.write("error", "pairing service command failed", { args, error: error.message, stderr })
              reject(error)
            },
          )
        }),
    )

    queue.tail = run.catch(() => undefined)

    return run
  }

  if (stored.value) keepScreenActive(true)
  ctx.scope.addFinalizer(release)

  ctx.provide(Pairing, {
    remote: async (_, caller) => (await service(["get", "remote"], caller.signal)) === "true",
    // Changing the setting stops the service. Starting it here brings it back, with the tunnel when remote access is
    // on. A window that closes meanwhile does not cancel the change.
    setRemote: async (enabled) => {
      await service(["set", "remote", String(enabled)], ctx.scope.signal)
      await service(["start"], ctx.scope.signal)
    },
    screenActive: () => blocker.id !== undefined && powerSaveBlocker.isStarted(blocker.id),
    setScreenActive: (enabled) => keepScreenActive(enabled),
  })
}

export default setup
```

### TextNode.deleteCharacters(start, end)

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

Deletes a range of characters between start and end indices within the text node. Requires fonts to be loaded before modification.

```APIDOC
### TextNode.deleteCharacters(start, end)

#### Description
Deletes characters spanning from the start index up to the end index.

#### Parameters
- **start** (`number`) - The zero-based character index at which deletion begins.
- **end** (`number`) - The zero-based character index at which deletion ends.

#### Example
```javascript
textNode.deleteCharacters(0, 6) // Delete first 6 characters
textNode.deleteCharacters(5, 10) // Delete characters 5-9
```
```

### Define start and end states with [*]

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/state.md

Uses [*] to represent both start and end states based on arrow direction. Multiple entries and exits are supported.

```mermaid
[*] --> Draft          // start transition
Published --> [*]      // end transition
```

### Define an Extension Setup Hook in Solid.js

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-extensions/README.md

Sets up extension lifecycle hooks, adds a SettingsPage, and registers an open command for desktop layout navigation. Lazy-loads settings page components on idle to prevent UI stutter.

```tsx
import { lazy, onCleanup, Suspense } from "solid-js"
import { onIdle, Command, SettingsPage, type Setup } from "../sdk"
import type definition from "./index"

const setup: Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.desktop) return
  const layout = ctx.layout
  const servers = ctx.servers
  const pairing = ctx.uses.pairing
  const Page = lazy(() => import("./page"))
  // Settings rows are small; load them while idle so settings opens without a blank row.
  onCleanup(onIdle(() => void Page.preload()))

  // The desktop's own server. Its ref is already authenticated in this window, so codes need no main process.
  const local = () =>
    servers
      .list()
      .map((id) => servers.get(id))
      .find((server) => server?.builtin)

  ctx.add(SettingsPage, {
    id: "pairing",
    icon: "server",
    available: "desktop",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("title")
    },
    get entries() {
      const pairingEntry = { id: "pairing", title: ctx.t("title"), keywords: "pair device qr phone remote" }

      // Remote access and the display setting exist only while pairing's main side answers.
      if (pairing().status !== "active") return [pairingEntry]

      return [
        pairingEntry,
        {
          id: "settings-remote-access",
          title: ctx.t("remote.title"),
          description: ctx.t("remote.description"),
          keywords: "internet tunnel opentunnel",
        },
        {
          id: "settings-keep-screen-active",
          title: ctx.t("screenActive.title"),
          description: ctx.t("screenActive.description"),
          keywords: "display sleep awake local",
        },
      ]
    },
    render: () => (
      <Suspense>
        <Page server={local} pairing={pairing} />
      </Suspense>
    ),
  })

  ctx.add(Command, {
    id: "open",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("command.title")
    },
    get group() {
      return ctx.t("command.category.server")
    },
    run: () => layout.settings("pairing"),
  })
}

export default setup
```

### Make a GET request to the running server

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/cli/commands.mdx

Sends a GET request to the running server's API. Use this to retrieve data from the server.

```bash
$ opencode api GET /api/session
```
